jscore.configuration.balance.hdd_latency: How long a hard disk drive takes to find what it is asked for, in ticks.
jscore.configuration.balance.nvme_latenc: How long an NVMe drive takes to find what it is asked for, in ticks.
jscore.configuration.balance.operation_p: How many ticks a queued Operation waits for each level of priority it gains; 0 never raises it.
jscore.configuration.balance.operation_w: How long an Operation waits on a locked resource or a busy machine before it gives up, in ticks.
jscore.configuration.balance.orphaned_op: How many hours a saved Operation nobody resumed waits before it is discarded; 0 keeps it for ever.
jscore.configuration.balance.program_mac: The real time one machine may spend running its programs in a tick, in microseconds.
jscore.configuration.balance.program_ser: The real time every machine together may spend running programs in a tick, in microseconds.
jscore.configuration.balance.ssd_latency: How long a solid-state drive takes to find what it is asked for, in ticks.
jscore.configuration.balance.subframe_ef: The share of its own capacity a Subframe lends the Mainframe it works for.
jscore.configuration.balance.tooltip: How the Operations engine waits and shares its work, and how long programs run.
jscore.configuration.calendar.days_per_s: How many days a season of the world's year lasts; a year is four seasons.
jscore.configuration.calendar.tooltip: The world's calendar: how long its seasons last.
jscore.configuration.config_version.tool: The version of this file's layout. The game upgrades an older file to it; leave it as it is.

The Geiger counter's size, in percent of the size it was drawn at.

The dosimeter's size, in percent of the size it was drawn at.
jscore.configuration.devices.tooltip: A corner and a size for each device carried.
jscore.configuration.diagnostics.count_n: Whether what the server sends each player is counted, for /jstech bandwidth.
jscore.configuration.diagnostics.stall_m: How long one piece of a mod's work may run before the watchdog writes down what it was doing, in milliseconds.
jscore.configuration.diagnostics.tooltip: The watchdog, and what the server counts of what it sends each player.
jscore.configuration.diagnostics.warn_op: Whether operators are told in chat when a piece of a mod's work stalls or slows itself.
Whether the air shimmers over hot things and the shockwave of an explosion bends the view.
jscore.configuration.effects.flash.toolt: How bright the screen flashes at an explosion or an arc: 0 for not at all, 1 as made.
jscore.configuration.effects.particles.t: How many particles the effects of the series may have at once on this game. When there are this many, the farthest emit fewer.
jscore.configuration.effects.shake.toolt: How hard the screen shakes near an explosion or a heavy machine: 0 for not at all, 1 as made.
jscore.configuration.effects.tooltip: Particles, the screen's shake and flash, heat haze and shockwaves.
jscore.configuration.elements.discoverer: Whether the player who first discovers an element beyond the 118 known gives it its name and its symbol, for everyone; when off, the series' own names are used.
jscore.configuration.elements.longest_na: How many letters a name given to an element may have.
jscore.configuration.elements.require_iu: Whether a name given to an element must end in -ium, as the elements' names do.
jscore.configuration.elements.tooltip: Naming the elements discovered beyond the 118 known.
jscore.configuration.energy.accept_any_v: Whether every block takes energy from a line of any class, as if it were its own.
jscore.configuration.energy.accept_fe.to: Whether the blocks of J's Energy take and give FE directly, both ways, with no converter, so the series speaks FE with the rest of a pack.
jscore.configuration.energy.electric_sho: Whether touching the bare wire of a live overhead line hurts, more the higher its class, and kills on high voltage and above.
jscore.configuration.energy.enabled.tool: Whether J's Energy is on, in joules, watts and voltage classes. Off, every block of the series takes and gives FE directly, as the rest of a pack does.
jscore.configuration.energy.joules_per_f: How many joules one FE is worth. At one, an FE a tick is 20 watts.
jscore.configuration.energy.lightning_su: Whether lightning on an overhead line or its pole sends a surge along the line, which burns the machines on it unless a fuse or a surge arrester stops it.
jscore.configuration.energy.overvoltage_: Whether a block on a line of a class above its port burns, or is ruined by an arc flash two classes up. Off, it just does not start.
jscore.configuration.energy.tooltip: J's Energy, the series' energy in joules, watts and voltage classes.
jscore.configuration.explosions.blocks_b: Blocks a blast breaks in a tick
How many blocks the blasts of a level break in a tick; the rest wait for the next ticks, so a great blast never stalls the server.
jscore.configuration.explosions.blocks_l: Blocks a blast looks at in a tick
How many blocks the blasts of a level look at in a tick, as their shock waves go out; a great blast past it goes on over the next ticks.
jscore.configuration.explosions.conseque: What each mod's explosions do to the world, by the mod's id or by one explosive's, as in "jsindustrial" = "spare_blocks": "full" breaks blocks, hurts and throws; "spare_blocks" hurts and throws but breaks nothing; "harmless" only flashes and sounds. An explosive's own setting comes before its mod's; one not named does it all.
jscore.configuration.explosions.show_gam: The game's explosions look the part
Whether the game's own explosions (TNT, creepers, beds in the Nether) show the fireball, the smoke, the sparks and the scorch marks the mods' blasts do. They break what they always did.
jscore.configuration.explosions.tooltip: What blasts do to the world, mod by mod, and how much of a tick they take.
jscore.configuration.fire.remains.toolti: Whether what burned stays burned: a log burns to charred wood and wool to ash, as data packs say, instead of vanishing.
jscore.configuration.fire.smoke.tooltip: Whether fires give off smoke that rises and drifts with the wind.
jscore.configuration.fire.tooltip: What fire does: the remains it leaves, the wind and the smoke.
jscore.configuration.fire.wind.tooltip: Whether the wind spreads a fire faster downwind and slower upwind, and a strong wind makes it leap a few blocks ahead.
Whether laws of physics that depart from ours (time at another pace, a pull that is not down, space that wraps) build up dissonance in a body, from warped sight to coming apart.
jscore.configuration.hazards.item_hazard: Whether what is carried harms its carrier: a hot ingot burns, sodium catches fire in the rain, a radioactive rod doses.
jscore.configuration.hazards.lungs.toolt: Whether coal dust, silica and asbestos breathed without a mask build up a lasting harm to the lungs.
jscore.configuration.hazards.mobs_suffer: Whether creatures suffer hazards as players do: animals sicken and die in a contaminated place.
jscore.configuration.hazards.natural_rad: Whether every mineral with uranium or thorium in it is naturally radioactive, at a low rate.
jscore.configuration.hazards.pollution.t: Whether there is pollution: soot, acid rain, heavy metals and carbon dioxide given off and doing what they do; radioactive fallout goes with radiation.
jscore.configuration.hazards.radiation.t: Whether there is radiation at all: off, no dose builds up, nothing is contaminated, no source gives any off and the instruments read nothing.
jscore.configuration.hazards.tooltip: The world's hazards: which of them there are.
jscore.configuration.hazards.withering.t: Whether the world shows contamination: grass dies, plants wither and crops stop growing where radiation or pollution is high, and come back slowly where it falls.
jscore.configuration.heat.boil_off.toolt: Whether a liquid kept colder than the place it is in, as liquid nitrogen is, boils off as the place's heat leaks into its tank, the faster the worse the tank is insulated.
jscore.configuration.heat.hot_surfaces_b: Whether a block hotter than 150 °C burns whoever stands against it, unless they resist fire.
jscore.configuration.heat.ignites.toolti: Whether a block hotter than 300 °C sets alight what burns against it, as fire spreads.
jscore.configuration.heat.overheating_da: Whether a machine hotter than it stands loses health while it is; it stops to cool either way.
jscore.configuration.heat.pipes_freeze.t: Whether a pipe of a liquid freezes and carries none of it where the place is colder than the liquid's melting point, unless the pipe is insulated.
jscore.configuration.heat.tooltip: What heat does to the world: pipes that freeze, cold liquids that boil off, machines that overheat, fires and burns.
jscore.configuration.lighting.bloom.tool: How strong the halo of bright lamps and glowing parts and the shaft of a spotlight are: 0 for none, 1 as made, 2 twice.
jscore.configuration.lighting.coloured.t: Whether light of a colour tints the world it lights: a red alarm lamp turns its room red.
jscore.configuration.lighting.dynamic.to: Whether a torch held, a mob on fire or a glowing creature lights the way as it moves. It is drawn on this game only, and changes nothing of the world.
jscore.configuration.lighting.reach.tool: How far from the player coloured light, dynamic light and glow are drawn, in blocks.
jscore.configuration.lighting.tooltip: Coloured light, dynamic light, glow and how far they reach.
jscore.configuration.mechanical.parts_br: Whether a shaft, a gear or another part with a rating breaks when the torque through it passes the rating. A shear pin shears either way.
jscore.configuration.mechanical.tooltip: What mechanical power does to the world: parts that break under overload.
jscore.configuration.media.download_kilo: How many kilobytes a second the server sends each player of the recordings they are about to hear.
jscore.configuration.media.max_file_mega: The biggest recording a player may bring, in megabytes; 0 takes none.
jscore.configuration.media.player_quota_: How much of the server's store the recordings one player brought may take, in megabytes; 0 sets no limit.
jscore.configuration.media.tooltip: The recordings players hear and bring: how much of the connection they take, and how big one may be.
jscore.configuration.media.upload_kiloby: How many kilobytes a second a player sends the server of a recording they bring.
jscore.configuration.moving_structures.m: Most blocks in a moving structure
How many blocks one moving structure may be made of; a structure of more is refused, saying why.
jscore.configuration.moving_structures.p: How much of a tick, in milliseconds, the physics of a dimension's moving structures may take; past it a structure waits a tick, and goes the next whatever the budget.
jscore.configuration.moving_structures.s: Whether a moving structure whose blocks are no longer all joined, its middle broken out, becomes as many structures as it now is, each going its own way; off, it holds together.
jscore.configuration.moving_structures.t: The moving structures: how big one may be, how much of a tick their physics may take, and whether one broken in two parts.
jscore.configuration.multiblock.blocks_p: How many blocks a second a tool that builds a multiblock for a player places, one at a time.
jscore.configuration.multiblock.build_re: How far from a multiblock's controller, in blocks, the player may walk while a tool builds it; past that it stops.
jscore.configuration.multiblock.tooltip: Building multiblocks for players: how fast, and how far from them.
jscore.configuration.notifications.do_no: Whether no notification comes on the screen or sounds; they are kept in the history all the same.
jscore.configuration.notifications.histo: How many notifications the history keeps; the oldest make way for new ones.
jscore.configuration.notifications.hold_: Whether, while not to be disturbed, the game's own toasts (advancements, recipes) are held too.
jscore.configuration.notifications.place: The corner of the screen notifications appear in: top_right, top_left, bottom_right or bottom_left.
jscore.configuration.notifications.silen: The kinds of notification that never come on the screen, by id.
The mods whose notifications never come on the screen, by id.
jscore.configuration.notifications.toolt: Where notifications appear, what is silenced, and the history.
jscore.configuration.persistor.tooltip: The Space Persistor, the series' chunk loader.
jscore.configuration.persistor.watts_per: What each chunk a Space Persistor keeps loaded costs in power, in watts (with J's Energy off, an FE a tick is 20 watts). 0 turns its energy use off entirely: it takes none, and has no port and no Protection tab.
jscore.configuration.protection.audit.to: Whether who used, changed or broke what another player owns is written down, for /jstech audit to read.
jscore.configuration.protection.audit_en: How many entries the audit log keeps; the oldest make way for new ones.
jscore.configuration.protection.robots_p: How many robots one player may have at once; 0 lets nobody have any.
jscore.configuration.protection.team_dam: Whether players on one team can hurt each other. While the teams are the game's scoreboard teams, a team's own friendly fire decides when this is off.
jscore.configuration.protection.tooltip: Who may hurt whom, what is written down of what players do to others' things, and how many of each thing one player may have.
Whether a block of a room's walls facing a greater difference in pressure than it stands bursts, as a weak window does under water.
jscore.configuration.rooms.decompression: Whether the air rushing out of a sealed room through a hole pulls items, mobs and players towards it.
jscore.configuration.rooms.fire_in_pure_: Whether any flame in a room whose air is mostly oxygen sets alight at once everything that burns round it, an inferno.
jscore.configuration.rooms.fire_needs_ox: Whether fire goes out, and will not light, where the air has too little oxygen, in a room or out in a dimension without it.
The largest sealed room, in blocks: a closed space larger than this is taken as open to the place round it.
Whether mobs that breathe, by their kind, suffocate in air they cannot breathe; the undead and golems do not breathe.
jscore.configuration.rooms.plants_need_a: Whether crops and saplings grow only where there is air.
jscore.configuration.step_aside.coloured: Whether the Core leaves coloured light and the glow of bright things to Shimmer when it is installed.
jscore.configuration.step_aside.connecte: Leave connected textures to Continuity or CTM
Whether the Core leaves the connected textures of resource packs to Continuity or CTM when one is installed. Off keeps the Core's own as well, and the two may then draw over each other.
jscore.configuration.step_aside.dynamic_: Leave dynamic light to another mod
Whether the Core leaves the light of what is held, what burns and what glows to LambDynamicLights or Sodium Dynamic Lights when one is installed.
jscore.configuration.step_aside.tooltip: Each system, and whether it steps aside while such a mod is installed.
jscore.configuration.styles.by_mod.toolt: A style for one mod's screens, over the one for every screen: mod id = "namespace:name".
jscore.configuration.styles.everything.t:
The style every screen of every mod is drawn in, as "namespace:name".
Empty leaves each screen in its own mod's default.
jscore.configuration.styles.tooltip: The styles screens are drawn in.
jscore.configuration.veins.density.toolt: How many times as dense each kind of vein is, by its id; its middle is at most wholly ore.
jscore.configuration.veins.enabled.toolt: Whether ores lie in veins about three chunks wide, dense at the middle and thinning outwards, instead of scattered; the game's scattered iron, copper and gold are taken away while they do. Only chunks made from then on change.
jscore.configuration.veins.rarity.toolti: How many times as often each kind of vein is found, by its id, as in "jscore:iron" = 0.5; 0 lays none of it. A kind not named keeps its own.
jscore.configuration.veins.spread.toolti: How many times as large each kind of vein is, by its id; a vein is never wider than its zone of three chunks.
jscore.configuration.veins.try_moving_ot: Try moving other mods' scattered ores into veins, finding them by the common ores tag. It works with mods that lay their ores as data, and may miss a mod that lays them its own way.
jscore.configuration.veins.without_ore.t: The materials whose ore is never laid, by their ids, as in "jscore:tin"; veins of them keep their other ores.
jscore.configuration.world.chunks_per_ow: How many chunks one player or team may keep loaded through machines, across every dimension; 0 lets nobody keep any.
jscore.configuration.world.chunks_server: How many chunks every player and team together may keep loaded through machines, across every dimension: the server's budget, besides each owner's own number; 0 lets nobody keep any.
jscore.configuration.world.tooltip: What machines may do to the world: how many chunks an owner keeps loaded.
jscore.configuration.world_events.disabl: The events that never happen by themselves, by their ids, as in "mymod:earthquake".
jscore.configuration.world_events.enable: Whether the events the mods declare (storms, showers, quakes) happen by themselves, by their schedules and their chances. An operator's command starts any of them still.
jscore.configuration.world_events.freque: How many times as often each event that happens by chance does, by its id, as in "mymod:solar_storm" = 0.5. An event not named keeps its own chance.
jscore.configuration.world_events.harmle: The events that leave the world as it is, by their ids: no craters, no radiation, no cracks. They still come, warn and play their effects.
jscore.configuration_card.corner: First corner marked: use the card on the opposite corner to paste over the box
jscore.configuration_card.empty: The card holds no setup: sneak and use it on a machine to copy one
jscore.configuration_card.how: Sneak and use on a machine to copy; use on machines to paste, or on two corners to paste over a box
jscore.configuration_card.nothing_fits: Nothing of this setup fits this machine, or it is not yours to set up
jscore.configuration_card.too_big: That box is too big: at most %s blocks
jscore.containment.sealed: No energy: sealed, it takes nothing and lets nothing out
jscore.converter.way.to_fe: Works from J's Energy to FE
jscore.converter.way.to_je: Works from FE to J's Energy

jscore.element.not_discovered: Element %s has not been discovered yet
jscore.element.not_discoverer: Only the player who discovered element %s names it
jscore.element.not_ium: In this world a name ends in -ium
jscore.element.not_named: Element %s has no name to take back
jscore.element.series_names: In this world elements keep the series' names
jscore.element.too_long: A name holds at most %s letters
jscore.element.unnamed: The name of element %s was taken back; its discoverer names it again
jscore.energy.damaged: Damaged: repair it to run again
jscore.energy.fuse_blown: Fuse blown: put in a new one
jscore.extinguisher.refills: Use it on water to fill it again
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.fix1: It has no energy: sealed, it lets nothing out, and nothing annihilates. Bring the energy back.
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.for: Keeping antimatter, which annihilates with any matter it touches and so fits in no other vessel.
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.get: The mods that keep antimatter in it, J's Industrial and J's Space, give it their recipes; in creative, take it from the J's Tech tab.
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.problem1: It takes nothing and gives nothing.
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.title: Antimatter Trap
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.use1: Lay a line to it and keep the energy coming: it spends it for as long as it holds antimatter.
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.use2: Fill and empty it by a line of exotic matter, from any side; it takes antimatter alone.
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.use3: Broken, it keeps what it holds in the item it drops; placed again, it holds it again.
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.value1_3: J's Energy at low voltage, or FE while J's Energy is off
jscore.guide.antimatter_trap.what: A Penning trap: a magnet's field and electrodes in a cold vacuum that hold antimatter away from every wall, as CERN keeps its antihydrogen.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.definit: A space walled in on every side by blocks that hold air. It keeps its own air: filled with oxygen it can be breathed on the Moon; a hole in it lets its air out.
The unit of pressure on the display, kPa. The air at sea level presses at about 101 kPa; a breath needs oxygen at more than 16 kPa of it.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.fix1: There is too little oxygen to breathe: fill the room with oxygen, or keep your helmet on.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.fix2: The room loses its air somewhere: show it in the world and close the leaks lit, a missing block, an open door or a pane.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.fix3: There is no air at all: the room is open to space, or was never filled.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.for: Knowing whether a room can be breathed before you take your helmet off, and finding where a room leaks its air.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.get: In creative, take it from the J's Tech tab; the mods that need it give it their recipes.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.title: Atmosphere Detector
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.use1: Place it in the room, or in its wall: a detector in a wall reads the room beside it.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.use2: Use it to open its screen. THE AIR lists each gas and its share, the pressure, and whether it is falling or rising.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.use3: THE ROOM draws the room from above, its leaks marked, with its size and how many leaks it has; OPEN AIR when no room holds it.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.use4: Press SHOW IN THE WORLD to see the room outlined round you, its leaks lit, while you walk it; press it again to stop.
jscore.guide.atmosphere_detector.what: A gauge for the air: it reads the air round it, a sealed room's or the open air's, and shows what it is made of, its pressure and the room it stands in.
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.fix1: A liquid too hot or too cold for it reached it for a while. Use the pipe made for it.
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.fix2: The pipe's end may be off, on another channel, or its filter may let nothing through.
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.for: Carrying liquids and gases from what makes them to what uses or keeps them.
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.get: Craft six of a row of glass panes between two rows of copper ingots, or of iron ingots for the gas pipe; four cryogenic pipes of iron, glass panes and obsidian. With J's Industrial installed, they are its first pipes, made with its own recipes.
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.problem1: A pipe bursts or cracks and spills.
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.title: Basic Pipes
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.use1: Lay a pipe from a machine's output to another's input: the machine pushes what it makes along it.
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.use2: Two tanks never pour into each other by themselves: set the end of the one to empty to pull, with the Basic Wrench.
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.use3: Each end can be set apart: its mode, its priority, its rate, its channel and its filter.
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.value1_1: Liquids up to 200 °C, 100 mB a tick
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.value1_2: Gases at low pressure, 100 mB a tick
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.value1_3: Liquids from the coldest up to 200 °C, 400 mB a tick
jscore.guide.basic_pipes.what: Three pipes, each holding its block alone, with a sight glass in each block that shows what flows inside at its level, moving the way it goes.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.fix1: Point at the wire itself, near the end you want; a part on the face closes it.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.fix2: It is someone else's: only its owner and whom they trust may set it up or take it.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.for: Setting how each end of a pipe or a line of items meets the block it plugs into.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.get: Craft it of four iron ingots: two at the top corners, two down the middle.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.problem2: A machine neither changes nor comes away.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.title: Basic Wrench
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.use1: Use it on the end of a wire, near the block it meets, to go round the modes.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.use2: Sneak to open the end's screen, on a pipe or a line of items: there the mode, the priority, the rate, the channel and the filter are set.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.use3: On any other line, sneak to go round the modes the other way.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.use4: The line says which end it set and how, above the hotbar.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.use5: While it is in your hand, what flows along the wire you look at, which way and how much, shows beside the crosshair.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.use6: On a machine, use it on a face to go round what that face does with the resource it shows: in, out, both or neither. While it is in your hand, each face of the machine you look at shows in its colour: blue in, amber out, green both, grey neither.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.use7: Sneak and turn the mouse wheel at a machine to show another of its resources.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.use8: Sneak and use it on a machine to take the machine away whole: its contents, upgrades, fuse, battery, settings and the work under way go with it. A pickaxe breaks it instead, and what it held falls out.
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.value1_1: As the block says: a machine's output gives, its input takes, a tank both
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.value1_2: The line only fills the block, and never draws from it
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.value1_3: The line only draws from the block, and never fills it
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.value1_4: The end plugs into nothing, and joins no cable beside it
jscore.guide.basic_wrench.what: An open-ended spanner of iron, the series' shared wrench.
jscore.guide.blank: This page is intentionally left blank.
jscore.guide.cable_block.fix1: Only cables of the same line join. An energy cable never joins a data cable, even in one block.
jscore.guide.cable_block.for: Running energy, data and the computers' peripheral cables through the same space, each kept to its own line.
jscore.guide.cable_block.get: Take a cable from a mod's creative tab: J's Industrial's Energy Cable, J's Computers' data and peripheral cables.
jscore.guide.cable_block.problem1: Two cables side by side do not join.
jscore.guide.cable_block.title: The cable block
jscore.guide.cable_block.use1: Place a cable like a block.
jscore.guide.cable_block.use2: Place a cable of another kind in the same block: it takes its own lane.
jscore.guide.cable_block.use3: Break the block to take its cables back, each one as its own item.
jscore.guide.cable_block.what: One block that every mod of the series lays its cables in. Each kind of cable runs in a lane of its own, so cables of different mods can share a block without touching.
jscore.guide.chapter.about: The library every mod of the series stands on. A player handles little of it: the materials the mods share, the energy they run on, the block their cables are laid in, and this manual.
jscore.guide.charred_wood_and_ash.fix1: The server turned off what fire leaves, in the balance settings.
jscore.guide.charred_wood_and_ash.for: Charred wood burns no more; it builds as wood does. Ash shows where a fire went.
jscore.guide.charred_wood_and_ash.get: They form by themselves where a fire burns wood and cloth away; break them to keep them.
jscore.guide.charred_wood_and_ash.title: Charred Wood and Ash
jscore.guide.charred_wood_and_ash.use1: Build with charred wood as with any wood; dig ash with a shovel.
jscore.guide.charred_wood_and_ash.what: What fire leaves: logs and planks charred black, and a layer of ash where cloth, leaves and thin wood burnt away.
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.fix1: Its dial is off, or what it was clamped on is gone. Turn the dial, or clamp it again.
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.fix2: Nothing crossed the wire yet, or it was clamped a moment ago; wait a second.
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.for: Finding where the energy goes, how much a line carries against its ceiling, and which machine draws it.
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.get: Take it from the creative tab J's Tech.
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.title: Clamp Meter
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.use1: Use it on a cable to clamp it on the energy wire you aim at.
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.use2: Use it on a machine or a store to read it face by face.
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.use3: Hold it: its reading shows beside the crosshair.
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.use4: Use it in the air to hold it up and read the details on its display.
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.value1_2: Shows the most and the least that crossed in a tick since it was clamped
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.value1_3: Shows the reading beside the crosshair while it is in hand
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.value1_5: Off, J's Energy's own units, or FE
jscore.guide.clamp_meter.what: A handheld instrument that reads energy. Clamped on a wire of a line, it reads what crosses the wire and which way; clamped on a machine or a store, what goes in and out of each of its faces.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.fix1: It is someone else's, or it has none of the resources copied: copy from a machine of the same kind.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.fix2: The box holds more than 4,096 blocks: mark a smaller one.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.for: Setting up many machines alike: a row of furnaces, a wall of crushers.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.get: Craft it of a sheet of paper, a redstone dust and a gold nugget.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.problem2: Pasting over a box does nothing.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.title: Configuration Card
jscore.guide.configuration_card.use1: Sneak and use it on a machine to copy its setup.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.use2: Use it on another machine to paste it: whole into one of the same kind, what fits into another.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.use3: Use it on a block that is not a machine, then on the opposite corner of a box: every machine in the box takes the setup at once.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.use4: Sneak and use it anywhere else to blank it.
jscore.guide.configuration_card.value1_1: What each face does with each resource, and what the machine pushes and pulls by itself, through which filter
jscore.guide.configuration_card.value1_2: How the machine answers redstone, and what a comparator reads of it
jscore.guide.configuration_card.value1_3: Its input slots' locks and the recipe picked, for a machine of the same kind only
jscore.guide.configuration_card.what: A card that remembers how a machine is set up.
jscore.guide.exotic_matter_containment.f: It has no energy: sealed, it lets nothing out, and nothing is lost. Bring the energy back.
Keeping the exotic matter the series' mods make or gather, which nothing else holds.
jscore.guide.exotic_matter_containment.g: The mods that keep exotic matter in it, J's Industrial and J's Space, give it their recipes; in creative, take it from the J's Tech tab.
jscore.guide.exotic_matter_containment.p: It takes nothing and gives nothing.
jscore.guide.exotic_matter_containment.u: Lay a line to it and keep the energy coming: it spends it for as long as it holds something.
Fill and empty it by a line of exotic matter, from any side.
Broken, it keeps what it holds in the item it drops; placed again, it holds it again.
jscore.guide.exotic_matter_containment.v: J's Energy at low voltage, or FE while J's Energy is off
jscore.guide.exotic_matter_containment.w: A heavy vessel whose field holds one exotic form of matter: neutronium, strange matter, dark matter and the rest, every one but antimatter.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.definition1: What burns: solids (wood, cloth), flammable liquids, electrical (something live with current), metals (sodium, magnesium) and cooking oils. Each takes its own agent.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.fix1: Water and foam carry the current: use carbon dioxide or dry powder.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.fix2: Water spreads a burning liquid or oil: use foam.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.fix3: Water on a burning metal makes it burst: only dry powder smothers it.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.fix4: Carbon dioxide leaves wood smouldering: finish it with water.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.for: Putting a fire out before it spreads, with the agent that suits what burns.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.get: In creative, take them from the J's Tech tab; the mods that need them give them their recipes.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.problem1: Spraying an electrical fire hurts you.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.problem2: The fire flares up round where you sprayed.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.title: Fire Extinguishers
jscore.guide.extinguishers.use1: Hold use and aim at the fire: it sprays a cone ahead, water farthest and carbon dioxide the shortest. Its bar shows what is left.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.use2: Water puts out solids; foam solids, liquids and cooking oils; carbon dioxide liquids and electrical fires, and leaves wood to smoulder; dry powder all but cooking oils.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.use3: Use a water extinguisher on water to fill it again.
jscore.guide.extinguishers.what: Red cylinders you spray on a fire, each of one agent, its band in the colour of the European code: water all red, foam cream, carbon dioxide black, dry powder blue.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.fix1: A line of another class meets its J's Energy side: set the class to the line's, or lay a line of the converter's class.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.fix2: More is offered than its limit lets through; turn the thumbwheels up, or use a converter of a higher class.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.for: Joining the series' lines to the machines and cables of any other mod, either way.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.get: Craft the low voltage one of iron, copper, redstone and gold, and each class above of the one below and dearer things. The configurable one is made from the ultra-high voltage one.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.problem1: The FAULT lamp is lit and nothing crosses.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.title: FE Converters
jscore.guide.fe_converters.use1: Facing its front, FE goes in or out on its left side and J's Energy on its right.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.use2: Turn the knob to choose the way: FE to JE, or JE to FE.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.use3: Set the most it moves on the thumbwheels: click a drum's upper half to turn it up, its lower half to turn it down, and the last drum for kilowatts, megawatts or gigawatts. It never goes above the class's ceiling.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.use4: On the configurable one, press a class key to set its class.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.use5: A joule is worth one FE unless the server sets otherwise; a converter rounds down, so it never makes energy.
jscore.guide.fe_converters.what: Cabinets that turn the game's FE into J's Energy, or J's Energy into FE: one of each voltage class, and the Configurable Energy Converter, whose class you set.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.definition1: The game's beat: 20 ticks make a second. 40 FE a tick is 800 FE a second.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.definition2: The energy a machine can store, like a small battery inside it. It keeps a machine working for a while after its power stops.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.fix1: It spends more a tick than its generators make. Add a generator.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.fix2: Nothing touches it and no cable runs from it. Join a machine to it.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.for: A generator makes it, a cable carries it, a machine spends it while it works.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.get: Make it with a generator, such as J's Industrial's Coal Generator.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.problem2: The generator burns fuel but nothing gets energy.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.title: Energy (FE)
jscore.guide.fe_energy.use1: Place a generator and give it fuel.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.use2: Put machines against it, or lay energy cable from it to them.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.use3: Watch a machine's energy bar: it fills while energy comes in.
jscore.guide.fe_energy.what: Energy is what machines and computers run on. It is counted in FE, the same unit most machine mods use, so a generator of another mod can run these machines and the other way round.
jscore.guide.fire_detectors.definition1: How much of the light the smoke takes away, in percent. A smoke detector calls at ten.
jscore.guide.fire_detectors.fix1: The fire is above it or too far to one side: hang it higher, over the fire.
jscore.guide.fire_detectors.for: Raising the alarm, or setting off anything you wire to them, when a fire starts.
jscore.guide.fire_detectors.get: In creative, take them from the J's Tech tab; the mods that need them give them their recipes.
jscore.guide.fire_detectors.title: Fire Detectors
jscore.guide.fire_detectors.use1: Place one under a ceiling above what might burn: smoke rises, so a fire above it is not seen.
jscore.guide.fire_detectors.use2: Each gives redstone on every side: full while it calls, or, chosen with a signal probe, the smoke or the temperature it reads.
jscore.guide.fire_detectors.what: Detectors hung under a ceiling: a smoke detector sees the smoke that rises to it, a heat detector feels the air reach 57 °C. Their lamp lights while they call.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.definition1: How fast radiation doses you where you stand, in millisieverts an hour (mSv/h). The ground gives off a little everywhere; near waste or a reactor it climbs.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.fix1: There is no radiation in this world: the server turned it off, or no mod gives it.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.fix2: The rate is past its scale: press RANGE, and get away.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.for: Knowing where radiation is before it doses you, and marking on your hazard map the chunks you walk through.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.get: In creative, take it from the J's Tech tab; the mods that need it give it their recipes.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.problem2: The needle is pinned at the right.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.title: Geiger Counter
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.use1: Keep it in your hotbar or your off hand: it shows on your screen and reads as you walk.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.use2: Use it to hold it up. RANGE reads ten and then a hundred times higher, for a place where the needle is pinned; SOUND turns its clicks off and on.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.use3: Where it shows on your screen, and how big, is in the hazard devices' settings.
jscore.guide.geiger_counter.what: A radiation meter in a yellow case: its needle and its figures show how much radiation comes at you where you stand, and it clicks faster as it climbs.
jscore.guide.hazard_map.definition1: A column of the world 16 blocks wide. The map knows only the chunks an instrument in your hands or a sensor on a network read; the rest stays grey.
jscore.guide.hazard_map.fix1: Nothing was measured here yet: walk the land with a Geiger counter in your hotbar.
jscore.guide.hazard_map.for: Seeing where it is safe to go, and where you measured last and how long ago.
jscore.guide.hazard_map.get: In creative, take it from the J's Tech tab; the mods that need it give it their recipes.
jscore.guide.hazard_map.title: Hazard Map
jscore.guide.hazard_map.use1: Hold it: it shows on your screen, live, with what is read here.
jscore.guide.hazard_map.use2: Use it to open the whole map. Pick the hazard with the buttons at the top; the legend says what each colour means. Click a chunk for its reading and its age; drag to look further.
jscore.guide.hazard_map.what: A handheld map of the land round you, each chunk coloured by the hazard read there: radiation, or a pollution.
jscore.guide.hold_to_open: Hold [%s] to open its page in the manual
jscore.guide.insulated_copper_cable.fix1: The line carries 10 kW at most, and loses some on the way; lay a second line, or keep it shorter.
jscore.guide.insulated_copper_cable.for: Carrying energy from what makes or keeps it to what spends it, block to block. While J's Energy is off, as it comes, it carries FE to any mod's machine.
jscore.guide.insulated_copper_cable.get: Craft six of a row of copper ingots between two rows of dried kelp. With J's Industrial installed, it is that mod's first cable, made with its own recipe.
jscore.guide.insulated_copper_cable.prob: The machine at the end gets less than it needs.
jscore.guide.insulated_copper_cable.use1: Lay it from a store or a generator to a machine.
jscore.guide.insulated_copper_cable.use2: A line longer than it needs loses more on the way: keep it short.
jscore.guide.insulated_copper_cable.valu: A tenth of what it carries over a hundred blocks
jscore.guide.insulated_copper_cable.what: The basic cable: a low voltage line of J's Energy, copper in black rubber, laid like every cable of the series in the shared cable block.
jscore.guide.lead_acid_battery_bank.fix1: It takes and gives through any face, but only by a line it is plugged into; lay a cable to it.
jscore.guide.lead_acid_battery_bank.for: Keeping energy for when nothing makes it, and smoothing what a line carries.
jscore.guide.lead_acid_battery_bank.get: Craft it of four iron ingots at the corners, a copper ingot above and below a water bucket, and redstone at its sides. With J's Industrial installed, it is that mod's first energy bank, made with its own recipe.
jscore.guide.lead_acid_battery_bank.use1: Place it on a line: it takes what the line has spare and gives it back when the line runs short.
jscore.guide.lead_acid_battery_bank.use2: The gauge on its sides shows how full it is, in four steps.
jscore.guide.lead_acid_battery_bank.what: The basic battery: cells of lead plates in acid, in a steel case, at low voltage.
This binder holds the reference for every mod of the series you have. Each has its chapter and its tab at the edge.

Every entry says, in this order, what the thing is, what it is for, how to get it, how to use it step by step, and what can go wrong. A figure (Figure 3-9) shows what a part looks like, a table (Table 3-7) gives its numbers, and a number after See (See 3.4.3) leads to another entry.
The magnifier on the top edge finds any part by name in the index. Hold the manual key over an item to open its page.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.fix1: The block is not a multiblock's controller. Use it on the controller itself.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.fix2: You ran out of a block, walked too far away, or a place is protected or taken. Its display says which; fix it and press OK again.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.for: Building a large multiblock without placing every block of it by hand.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.get: In creative, take it from the J's Tech tab; the mods that build multiblocks give it their recipes.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.problem1: It says this controller forms no multiblock it knows.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.title: Multiblock Builder
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.use1: Place the multiblock's controller, then use the builder on it: it is aimed at it, and its display shows what is missing and what you have.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.use2: On the page of choices, choose with the arrows what goes where a place takes several blocks.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.use3: Press OK: it builds, a block at a time, as you would place them. HOLD holds it and carries it on.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.use4: SHOW shows the multiblock's ghosts while you hold it; LIGHT lights its display.
jscore.guide.multiblock_builder.what: A handheld instrument that builds a multiblock around its controller for you, block by block, from your inventory: it says what it will place and how much of each you have, and asks what goes where a place takes several blocks.
jscore.guide.network_probe.fix1: The wire it was linked to was taken out, or its chunk is far away; link it again.
jscore.guide.network_probe.for: Finding what a line joins, what flows along it, where it is too narrow and what it loses on the way.
jscore.guide.network_probe.get: Take it from the creative tab J's Tech.
jscore.guide.network_probe.problem1: The display says there is nothing to read.
jscore.guide.network_probe.title: Network Probe
jscore.guide.network_probe.use1: Use it on a wire of a line to link it to that line.
jscore.guide.network_probe.use2: Use it in the air to hold it up and read its display; the keys under the display turn its pages.
jscore.guide.network_probe.use3: On the members' page, choose a row with the pad and press OK: those blocks are outlined in the world, through walls, for ten seconds.
jscore.guide.network_probe.use4: HOLD keeps the reading still, SHOW puts it beside the crosshair while you hold it, LIGHT lights the display and POWER switches it off.
jscore.guide.network_probe.value1_1: The flow of the last minute against the narrowest cable, what the consumers want, the losses, and how many sources, consumers and stores it joins
jscore.guide.network_probe.value1_2: Every block it plugs into, by what it is to the line and by kind, with what each gives or takes
jscore.guide.network_probe.value1_3: Each second of the last minute, with the most, the least and the mean
jscore.guide.network_probe.value1_4: What the cables lost, against what the sources sent
jscore.guide.network_probe.what: A handheld instrument in an orange holster that reads a whole line at once, of any kind: energy, liquids, gases or items.
jscore.guide.no_command: This page is missing: no mod answers for the command %s.
jscore.guide.no_recipes: No recipe of this kind is loaded in this world.
jscore.guide.nowhere_back: Nowhere yet: follow a link, a tab or the contents first
jscore.guide.pocket_dosimeter.definition: The unit of a dose, Sv. About one sievert brings a mild sickness, Rad I; eight and more come close to deadly, Rad V.
jscore.guide.pocket_dosimeter.fix1: You reached a band of radiation sickness: get away from the sources, and your body heals slowly.
jscore.guide.pocket_dosimeter.for: Knowing how much more you can take before you have to rest away from the sources.
jscore.guide.pocket_dosimeter.get: In creative, take it from the J's Tech tab; the mods that need it give it their recipes.
jscore.guide.pocket_dosimeter.title: Pocket Dosimeter
jscore.guide.pocket_dosimeter.use1: Carry it anywhere on you: it shows on your screen.
jscore.guide.pocket_dosimeter.use2: Use it to hold it up; LIGHT lights its face for the dark.
jscore.guide.pocket_dosimeter.what: A small meter you carry: it shows the dose of radiation your body has taken, and the band of radiation sickness it reached.

jscore.guide.shared_materials.fix1: Only the recipes the machine knows take it. Dust is smelted, not pressed.
jscore.guide.shared_materials.for: Every mod uses the same ones, so the iron plate one mod makes is the iron plate another asks for. Only the forms some installed mod uses are in the game, and later machines and parts are made from them.
jscore.guide.shared_materials.get: Make them with the machines of J's Industrial, or take them from its creative tab, where they are shown.
jscore.guide.shared_materials.problem1: A dust will not go into a machine.

jscore.guide.shared_materials.value1_2: From an iron ingot, in a Compressor

jscore.guide.signal_probe.fix1: Its transmitter is too far, behind too much wall, or its chunk is not loaded; frequencies of your team show as lost, others are not listed at all.
jscore.guide.signal_probe.for: Reading the redstone on a wire, and finding which frequencies are heard where you stand: whose they are, where they come from, how well they arrive and what they carry.
jscore.guide.signal_probe.get: Take it from the creative tab J's Tech.
jscore.guide.signal_probe.problem1: A frequency you expect is not listed.
jscore.guide.signal_probe.title: Signal Probe
jscore.guide.signal_probe.use1: Use it on a block, a redstone wire or any other, to read the redstone on it.
jscore.guide.signal_probe.use2: Use it in the air to hold it up and read its display; the keys under the display turn its pages.
jscore.guide.signal_probe.use3: Walk with it to find where a receiver or a relay will hear a frequency well: each solid block in the way shortens a transmitter's reach.
jscore.guide.signal_probe.use4: On the radio's page, choose a frequency with the pad and press OK: where it comes from is outlined in the world, through walls, for ten seconds.
jscore.guide.signal_probe.use5: HOLD keeps the reading still, SHOW puts it beside the crosshair while you hold it, LIGHT lights the display and POWER switches it off.
jscore.guide.signal_probe.value1_1: The strength on the wire it reads, out of 15, with its peak since you linked it, and the frequencies heard where you stand
jscore.guide.signal_probe.value1_2: The frequencies again, one chosen and told in full: its owner, where it comes from, its bars and its value
jscore.guide.signal_probe.value2_1: How well it arrives, from one at the edge of its reach to four close by; the value arrives whole with any bar
jscore.guide.signal_probe.value2_2: Two transmitters of one owner on one frequency: its receivers give nothing until one is taken off
jscore.guide.signal_probe.value2_3: A frequency of your team that is not heard where you stand
jscore.guide.signal_probe.what: A handheld instrument of the network probe's family, for redstone and for signals sent without wire by frequency.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.definition1: A column of the world 16 blocks wide. The game loads the chunks near players and lets the rest go; a machine in a chunk let go stops.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.fix1: You keep as many chunks as you may, or the server keeps as many as its budget allows. Take chunks off here or elsewhere.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.fix2: It is switched off, short of power, or has nothing to keep: feed it, switch it on, or check its area.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.for: Keeping machines working far from you, as far as you want to reach, within the number of chunks you may keep and the server's budget.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.get: In creative, take it from the J's Tech tab; the mods that need it give it their recipes.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.title: Space Persistor
jscore.guide.space_persistor.use1: Place it: it is yours, and keeps a square of three by three chunks round it.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.use2: Use it to open its screen. The map shows the land round it, the chunks it keeps outlined, another owner's hatched; zoom out with the minus.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.use3: Pick a shape with the keys (a square, a circle, a line or only what you click) and turn the radius' drums to reach further.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.use4: Click a chunk on the map to add it, or take it off.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.use5: When the server makes it spend energy, feed it power; its Protection tab holds a fuse and a battery as every machine's does.
jscore.guide.space_persistor.what: A chunk loader: it keeps an area round it loaded and working while nobody is near, so a quarry far away, a station or a starship left in orbit goes on.
jscore.guide.sprinkler.fix1: It has no water: check its pipe.
jscore.guide.sprinkler.fix2: Water is wrong for burning liquids, oils and metals: watch those with a detector instead.
jscore.guide.sprinkler.for: Putting out a fire in a room by itself, while nobody is there.
jscore.guide.sprinkler.get: In creative, take it from the J's Tech tab; the mods that need it give it their recipes.
jscore.guide.sprinkler.problem2: The fire it showers flares up or bursts.
jscore.guide.sprinkler.title: Sprinkler
jscore.guide.sprinkler.use1: Place it under a ceiling and run a water pipe to it, or put a tank beside it: it holds a bucket and draws more from the pipe.
jscore.guide.sprinkler.use2: It showers a hundred millibuckets a second while it is open, and shuts half a minute after the heat is gone.
jscore.guide.sprinkler.what: A sprinkler head hung under a ceiling: its red glass bulb bursts at 68 °C, the heat of a fire below, and it showers the place under it.
jscore.guide.structure_projector.definit: A pale, see-through block where a block of the multiblock still goes. Look at one to see which block and on which layer.
jscore.guide.structure_projector.fix1: Its switch is off, no multiblock is chosen, or you are more than 64 blocks away.
jscore.guide.structure_projector.fix2: Another block stands there. Break it and place the one the ghost shows.
jscore.guide.structure_projector.for: Building a multiblock right the first time, block by block, without counting layers from a picture.
jscore.guide.structure_projector.get: In creative, take it from the J's Tech tab; the mods that build multiblocks give it their recipes.
jscore.guide.structure_projector.problem: A block stays outlined in red.

jscore.guide.structure_projector.use2: Use it to open its screen and choose the multiblock from the list.
jscore.guide.structure_projector.use3: Turn it with the knob, mirror it if it allows, and show it a layer at a time with the layer's wheel, or only what is still missing.
jscore.guide.structure_projector.use4: Build into the ghosts: each goes as its block is placed, and the count above follows.
jscore.guide.structure_projector.what: A projector that shows any multiblock of any mod you have in the world, before you build it: the blocks still missing as pale ghosts, a wrong block outlined in red, and above the structure how much is in place.

jscore.hazard.dissonance.treatment: Go back to normal laws, or stand in a bubble of them
jscore.hazard.heavy_metal_poisoning.trea: Chelation draws the metals out; stop eating what grew on fouled ground

jstech.guide.chapter.about: What every mod of the series shares: the eras computers come in, the tiers machines come in, and the network that joins them all.
jstech.guide.data_network.definition1: A request the network carries out: store this, give me that, craft this. Every one waits in a queue on the Mainframe until it is done.
jstech.guide.data_network.fix1: A network has one Mainframe. Split the cables, so that each Mainframe has a network of its own.
jstech.guide.data_network.for: A network stores items as data on its disks, gives them back when asked, moves them between machines and crafts for you. Machines of other mods of the series join it through the same cables.
jstech.guide.data_network.get: Build a Mainframe from J's Computers, and lay data cables from it to the machines that should join.
jstech.guide.data_network.title: The network
jstech.guide.data_network.use1: Build the Mainframe and give it its parts.
jstech.guide.data_network.use2: Lay data cable from it to a Server Rack with servers and disks, where the items are kept.
jstech.guide.data_network.use3: Join a computer to the network and open its Network program to put items in and take them out.
jstech.guide.data_network.what: The network is computers joined by data cables around one large computer, the Mainframe. Each network has exactly one Mainframe, and every machine on it shares its name.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.definition1: How many bits a processor works with at once: 16 in the Vintage, 32 in the Legacy, 64 from the Transition on. On a network's disks it decides how much room an item takes.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.fix1: It is from another era than the motherboard. Use a part of the board's era.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.fix2: The system is from a newer era than the computer. Use an older system, or newer hardware.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.for: Eras are how computers grow: a newer era is faster at everything, with more cores at higher clocks, more memory and faster disks, and it runs newer systems and programs.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.get: Each era has its own creative tab in J's Computers, from J's Computers - Vintage to J's Computers - Advanced, with the same shelves in each.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.problem1: A part does not go into the computer at all.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.table1: The eras that have hardware today
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.title: Eras of hardware
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.use1: Pick an era and build everything of it: a computer of an era takes only a motherboard of its own era, and the board takes only parts of its era.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.use2: Install a system of that era or an older one: a system needs hardware of its own era or newer.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.use3: Move up an era when you want more speed; the old machines keep working beside the new.
jstech.guide.hardware_eras.what: An era is a generation of computing hardware, from the Vintage, like the machines of the early 1990s, to the Advanced, like the machines of today. Every computer and every part belongs to one.
jstech.guide.industrial_tiers.fix1: It belongs to a tier that has no machines yet. It comes with a later update.
jstech.guide.industrial_tiers.for: Tiers set the order things are reached in, from the first machines that run on coal to the last ones. They are a different scale from the eras: an era says how new a computer is, a tier how far industry has come.
jstech.guide.industrial_tiers.get: There is nothing to take: tiers are reached by making things. Today the first tiers have content; the higher ones come with later updates.
jstech.guide.industrial_tiers.problem1: A material shows in a list but cannot be made.
jstech.guide.industrial_tiers.title: Industrial tiers
jstech.guide.industrial_tiers.use1: Start with the machines of the first tier: the Coal Generator, the Macerator, the Compressor and the Electric Furnace.
jstech.guide.industrial_tiers.use2: Use what they make, dust and plates, to reach what needs them.
jstech.guide.industrial_tiers.what: A tier is a step of industry, from T0 to T9: how hard a material or a machine is to make, and what has to exist before it can be made.
